overview: Rapid review of pharmacist-led follow-up for adults starting oral anticancer agents, with separate strands for harms, adherence, and time and money.
population: Studies and reports of adults starting oral anticancer agents, 2010 onward, English only.
exposure: Pharmacist-led follow-up in the first weeks of oral treatment.
procedures: Library searches of three databases and agency websites; one screener with a 20 percent check; data extraction by one pharmacist, verified by the second for key outcomes.

outcomes.name: Unplanned toxicity admissions and severe toxicity
outcomes.measure: Proportion admitted for toxicity or with grade 3 or worse toxicity within 90 days, as reported
outcomes.why: Patient-important and the basis of any saving.

outcomes.name: Service cost and admission costs averted
outcomes.measure: Annual service cost and reported averted admission costs, as ranges

outcomes.name: Adherence by measurement method
outcomes.measure: Adherence as reported, tabulated separately for pill count, refill, electronic cap and self-report

outcomes.name: Relative dose intensity
outcomes.timing: First three cycles or as reported
outcomes.why: Fewer toxicities may come with less treatment (claim c4).

outcomes.name: Pharmacist time per patient
outcomes.measure: Hours per patient over the first 12 weeks

feasibility: Two pharmacists at six hours a week each to 29 January 2027.
biasMitigation: Costs reported as ranges with assumptions

biasFlags.label: Single screening
biasFlags.note: 20 percent check by a second reviewer.

flags: Economic outcome labelled with its own role
parsimony.simplestPath: One question per strand, one extraction form.

summary: Rapid review protocol with a primary harm outcome and a cost outcome under an economic role.
